newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres 1996 net helped by units.
newsitem.headline: Benpres 1996 net helped by units.

text.p: Benpres Holdings Corp said on Wednesday its net income in 1996 was helped by the continued profitability of affiliate companies.

Earlier, it reported its audited net income in 1996 rose by 25 percent to two billion pesos from 1.6 billion pesos in 1995. Group revenues expanded by 31 percent to 5.4 billion from 4.1 billion pesos.
Xavier Gonzales, the firm's chief operating officer, said "the earnings met the company's medium-term earnings growth target of 25 percent."
Its 71-percent owned ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp contributed to 53 percent of total earnings.
Its interests in power generation and distribution accounted for 24 percent of earnings, while other concerns comprised the rest.
Its 25-percent owned First Philippine Holdings Corp concentrated on energy development and started looking into the development of industrial parks, Benpres said in a statement.
Philippine Commercial International Bank, in which Benpres has an 18 percent stake, remained at the top tier of the banking system.
Its telecom affiliate, Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Corp, ended its first full year of operation with the successful installation of 336,000 lines for its local exchange network.
Its 50 percent-owned First Philippine Infrastructure Development Corp completed last year the 8.8-kilometre segment of its toll road project in the northern part of the main island if Luzon.

Rafael Andrada, the firm's chief finance officer, earlier told Reuters Benpres' telecommunications project is expected to start contributing to the bottomline in 1998, and its toll roads and water projects in 2000.
